items.title: An Evidence-Grounded Framework for Evaluating AI-Generated Educational Feedback
items.abstract: Educational feedback generated by artificial intelligence is becoming more and more popular in teaching, but there are still differences in how to evaluate its quality in existing research. This study examined 68 empirical studies and compared the criteria, methods, evaluators, and evidence used in these evaluations. The results show that the relevant evaluation can be roughly summarised into three dimensions: Evidence Validity, Rubric and Task Alignment, and Pedagogical Usefulness. Evidence Validity focuses on whether the feedback is accurate and reliable, and is based on the learner's actual work. Rubric and Task Alignment focuses on whether the feedback meets the task requirements, evaluation criteria, and learner responses. Pedagogical Usefulness focuses on whether the feedback is clear, specific, actionable, and can support revision and further learning. The reviewed studies also used a variety of evidence to judge the quality of feedback, including human judgement, learner perceptions, revision behaviour, learning outcomes, and automated metrics. Based on these findings, this study proposes an evaluation framework that links different dimensions of feedback quality with corresponding evidence to provide clearer evaluation ideas for subsequent research and educational practice.

items.title: An explainable hybrid CNN-transformer framework for multi-representation leukaemia classification
items.abstract: Acute Lymphoblastic Leukaemia (ALL) is a severe form of hematologic cancer that requires precise and prompt diagnosis for improved survival rates of patients. The conventional technique of examining microscopic images of peripheral blood smears is quite subjective, laborious, and heavily reliant on expert opinion. However, recent developments in artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML), specifically deep learning, have made automated detection of leukaemia possible; but the available techniques are biased due to training datasets, lack generalizability and are poorly interpretable. This paper presents a novel Hybrid Deep Learning Approach for Multi-Class Classification of Acute Lymphoblastic Leukaemia using EfficientNet and ViT Models. The framework uses convolutional networks for feature extraction, transformer networks for global representation learning, and handcrafted features. We evaluate the method on two clinical datasets: ALL-IDB2 and the ALL Image Dataset from Kaggle, both of which include benign and malignant types (Benign, Early, Pre, Pro). The comparison with benchmark methods shows that the proposed approach outperforms others. To improve model interpretability, we used Grad-CAM visualisations and Vision Transformer attention maps to examine image regions associated with the model’s predictions, complemented by quantitative faithfulness analysis. The proposed model achieves strong accuracy, F1-scores, specificity, and Matthews Correlation Coefficient (MCC). Although the framework demonstrated strong performance on both datasets, patient-wise separation could not be independently verified because reliable patient identifiers were not consistently available; therefore, further patient-wise and multi-centre external validation is required. These findings demonstrate the potential of the proposed explainable hybrid framework for accurate and interpretable leukaemia classification.

items.abstract: This study aims to describe the profile of non-academic giftedness in a university student who demonstrates outstanding abilities in graphic design. The research employed a qualitative approach using a single case study design. Data were collected through in-depth interviews, portfolio observations, and documentation of organizational activities. The findings reveal that the subject exhibits giftedness characterized by high visual-spatial cognitive ability, strong creativity, high intrinsic motivation and task commitment, well-developed socio-emotional skills, and refined psychomotor abilities. These findings support Clark’s multidimensional model of giftedness, emphasizing that non-academic giftedness can develop optimally when supported by personal motivation and a conducive environment. The study highlights the importance of recognizing and nurturing creative talents in higher education settings.

items.title: Analysing Mathematical Communication between Pre-Service Mathematics Teachers and GenAI: A Case Study in Abstract Algebra Course
items.abstract: Background The emergence of Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI), particularly ChatGPT, offers new possibilities for mathematics learning in higher education. Although ChatGPT can provide explanations, examples, guiding questions, and feedback, its use in Abstract Algebra courses has largely been limited to answering questions and verifying mathematical answers or proofs. This study analyses pre-service mathematics teachers’ mathematical communication when interacting with ChatGPT through seven indicators, including: interpreting formal definitions; using mathematical terms, symbols, variables, and notation appropriately; constructing examples, non-examples, and counter-examples; explaining relationships between algebraic objects and their properties; justifying arguments or proofs; evaluating the validity of mathematical responses; and formulating coherent conclusions. Method A qualitative case study involved 18 pre-service mathematics teachers enrolled in an Abstract Algebra course in the department of mathematics education at a public university in Bandung City, West Java, Indonesia. Data comprised written dialogues between the pre-service mathematics teachers and ChatGPT while solving Abstract Algebra problems and were analysed using the seven indicators. Results The findings indicate that the pre-service mathematics teachers’ mathematical communication generally ranged from developing to adequate. They performed relatively well in using terminology and notation, constructing examples or counter-examples, and explaining relationships among algebraic objects and properties. However, justification, critical evaluation of ChatGPT responses, and independent conclusion-making remained weak. While some pre-service mathematics teachers accepted inaccurate AI responses, others identified and connected them. Conclusion The findings suggest that GenAI should serve as a dialogue partner and scaffolding, rather than an authority on mathematical truth. Mathematics course should emphasise verification, justification, critical evaluation, and argument reconstruction to foster independent mathematical communication skills.

items.title: AnomalyJev: Towards Evaluating Image Anomaly Explanations via Claim-Level Verification
items.abstract: Recent multimodal LLM (MLLM)-based anomaly detection (AD) methods can generate textual explanations that help interpret their predictions. However, reliably and efficiently evaluating these explanations remains challenging. While LLM judges can assess explanations through structured rubrics, they often require substantial token generation, making evaluation costly and difficult to scale. We instead propose to anchor evaluation in the available ground truth by extracting verifiable claims from each explanation and verifying them against the corresponding annotations. We instantiate this idea as AnomalyJev, a lightweight framework that extracts verifiable claims from contextualised representations using ground-truth-defined queries and pointer based heads, without token generation. The claims are then verified against the ground truth to score faithfulness and completeness. For evaluation, we construct a human-annotated set of 640 explanations with over 1,600 expert ratings across in-domain and cross-dataset settings. Despite its compact design, AnomalyJev achieves stronger agreement with human annotators than most open MLLM judges and approaches that of flagship MLLM judges, at a fraction of their runtime and resources.

items.title: Application of Chemistry Achievement Test for Secondary School Students Using Developed ChatGPT Artificial intelligence and Traditional methods
items.abstract: This study was on Application of Chemistry Achievement Test for Secondary School Students Developed Using ChatGPT Artificial intelligence and Traditional methods. Three research questions and were formulated to guide the study. The instrumentation research design was used for the study. The population of the study consisted of all 11,594 Senior Secondary School Two (SSII) students from all the 187 public secondary schools in Akwa Ibom State. Multistage sampling procedure was used for the study. The sample of 387 SSII Students was used for the study. Data was collected using two researcher developed instruments named, “Chemistry Achievement Test On Chemical Equilibrium Developed using ChatGPT Method (CATCEDCM) and Chemistry Achievement Test On Chemical Equilibrium Developed using Traditional Method (CATCEDTM)”. The reliability coefficients of CATCEDCM and CATCEDTM were .992 and .971 determined using Split Half Method of reliability determination. The research questions were answered mean and standard deviation statistics while the independent t-test statistics was used to test the formulated null hypotheses at .05 alpha level. The findings of the study revealed that Students had higher achievement scores on Chemistry Achievement Test on Chemical Equilibrium developed using ChatGPT Artificial Intelligence than same test developed using traditional method. It was also revealed male and female Students had the same achievement scores on Chemistry Achievement Test on Chemical Equilibrium developed using ChatGPT Artificial Intelligence. Recommendations were made among others that Chemistry teachers should always make use ChatGPT artificial intelligence over the traditional method when developing a test since it could produce a test that appropriately assess students’ academic achievement.

items.title: Applications of Artificial Intelligence in Microbial Bioremediation: Current Advances, Challenges and Future Prospects
items.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is increasingly applied to microbial bioremediation to manage complex relationships among microorganisms, pollutants and environmental conditions. This critical narrative review examines peer-reviewed literature published from 1 January 2020 to the final search date of 21 September 2026 and evaluates AI across a pathway extending from microorganism and enzyme selection to pollutant-removal prediction, process optimization, experimental validation and real-world translation. Recent studies show that machine learning can identify microbial indicators, predict attenuation and removal of heavy metals and organic contaminants, optimize petroleum-, phenol- and PCB-degrading systems, and mine genomic or metagenomic data for candidate enzymes. However, the evidence base remains uneven because datasets are often heterogeneous, models may overfit, external validation is limited, and computational associations do not necessarily establish biological causation. The review therefore distinguishes computational prediction from biochemical, whole-cell, consortium, realistic-matrix and field validation. It argues that the most useful future pathway is an iterative prediction-validation-optimization framework in which AI prioritizes biological candidates and operating conditions, experiments confirm or reject predictions, and monitoring or field observations refine models. AI should consequently be viewed as a decision-support layer that strengthens, rather than replaces, microbiological understanding and experimental validation.

items.title: Applying Artificial Intelligence To Classify Urban Noise Sources From Smartphone Recordings: A Small-Scale Pilot Study In Hanoi
items.abstract: Conventional noise monitoring reports sound levels but not their sources, while dedicated sensor networks are costly. This paper presents a low-cost pipeline, from smartphone recording to noise-source classification and web-based monitoring, together with the results of a small-scale pilot in Hanoi. The data comprise 14 GPS-tagged recordings (14.7 minutes in total, 9 recording sessions) covering 8 source classes, including sounds specific to Vietnamese cities such as waste-collection gongs and street-vendor calls. Labels were taken from file names and verified by listening to 111 sample clips, with no labelling error found. Each recording was split in time: the first 70% for training and the last 30% for testing, with data augmentation applied to the training part only. Five models from three families were compared: SVM and Random Forest on MFCC features, a compact CNN on log-Mel spectrograms, and two classifiers on embeddings from the pretrained YAMNet model. On 113 test clips cut from the end of each recording (E1), four models reached accuracies of 0.956–0.991. However, when tested on recordings entirely unseen during training (E2, leave-one-recording-out), the MFCC-based models dropped to 0.363–0.467, whereas the YAMNet-based models retained 0.730-0.779. The CNN trained from scratch did not converge on this amount of data (E1 accuracy 0.204). The YAMNet + Dense model was integrated into a monitoring prototype (FastAPI, SQLite, a browser-based recording page and dashboard). Replaying the 113 test clips through the system API yielded an accuracy of 0.956, identical to the offline result, with a mean processing time of 76.7 ms per clip on a laptop without a GPU. The results show the feasibility of the pipeline and the advantage of transfer learning with little data, and highlight that evaluation within the same recordings is markedly optimistic compared with evaluation on new recordings.

items.title: Artificial Emotional Intelligence
items.abstract: Artificial Emotional Intelligence (AEI) refers to Artificial Intelligence (AI) systems that mediate human affect by sensing, processing, and responding to emotional states through multimodal inputs, including text, voice, and physiological signals (Chen et al. 2024 ). As AI systems (especially generative AI) become more conversational, personalised, and multimodal, AEI increasingly mediates therapy, companionship, customer service, education, and work (De Freitas et al. 2026 ; Zao-Sanders 2026 ). This marks a shift from mediating information and behaviour to mediating affect in sensitive contexts: AEI already underpins chatbots designed to mitigate suicide risk (Maples et al. 2024 ), customer-service systems that respond to frustration (Fan et al. 2024 ), and personalised sexbot applications (Rubinsztein and Ciriello 2024 ). This shift reflects technical progress, but also intensifies concerns about social fragmentation, care-capacity gaps, and the expansion of monetisation-oriented platform logics into domains historically organised around care, trust, and professional duty (Arsel 2026 ; Leong et al. 2021 ; Seleznova et al. 2023 ). Despite its significance, this reconfiguration of digital intermediation remains under-conceptualised in Information Systems (IS) research.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence and Job Design: A Dynamic Framework
items.abstract: This study aims to deepen the understanding of artificial intelligence's (AI) impact on work by introducing and describing the AI-Job Dynamics Framework. Drawing from sociotechnical systems theory, complexity theory, and organizational learning theories, we conceptualize AI integration as a dynamic, non-linear process with three key phases. The framework, supported by theoretical propositions, identifies how this process affects organizational decision-making structures and key job characteristics over time, emphasizing the balance between centralization and decentralization of decision-making power. AI integration initially reduces job autonomy but may lead to greater autonomy in later phases as AI becomes more embedded. Throughout this process, AI reshapes skill requirements from routine to complex cognitive and adaptive skills. In the advanced phase of AI integration, we introduce the alternative paths and varied trajectories through which AI, organizational structures, and individual work experiences evolve. We conclude by discussing the implications of this framework for future research on AI and job design.

items.title: Artificial intelligence and machine learning for magnetic nanoparticles and nanocarriers in cancer imaging, drug delivery, and magnetic control: a systematic review
items.abstract: We reviewed artificial intelligence and machine learning in magnetic resonance imaging-visible magnetic nanoparticles, nanocarriers, and systems for imaging, drug delivery, hyperthermia, targeting, transport, and control. Using “preferred reporting items for systematic reviews and meta-analyses (PRISMA) 2020” methods, 2,283 records from seven databases yielded 65 studies. Predicted outcomes were colloidal stability, toxicity, uptake, magnetic descriptors, specific absorption rate, relaxivity, MRI signal, superparamagnetic iron oxide nanoparticle (SPION) quantification, drug release, biodistribution, and magnetic navigation. Evidence was strongest in bounded tasks: magnetic-property and relaxivity prediction, image-derived SPION mapping, hyperthermia modelling, and controlled magnetic transport. Most studies optimised isolated endpoints rather than integrating stability, MRI visibility, drug loading, release, tumour delivery, safety, and therapeutic response. External validation across datasets, laboratories, particle batches, biological models, scanners, and patient cohorts remains limited.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning in Composite Manufacturing: Recent Advances, Emerging Trends, Digital Twins, and Future Perspectives
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) are revolutionizing composite manufacturing by enabling data-driven forecasts, process optimization, defect identification, and intelligent process control. The objective of this review is to discuss the recent innovations and emerging trends in the application of AI/ML in the major composite manufacturing technologies, such as automated fiber placement (AFP), automated tape laying (ATL), resin transfer molding (RTM), resin infusion, compression molding, pultrusion, additive manufacturing, and non-destructive evaluation (NDE). This paper discusses the capabilities and limitations of advanced technologies, including deep learning, physics-informed machine learning, transfer learning, multimodal learning, explainable AI, digital twin, surrogate modeling, and closed-loop control, and their future potential. A comprehensive literature survey explored the latest developments in composite manufacturing using AI/ML. The review categorized the research by manufacturing process, AI/ML approach, sensor and inspection modality, prediction and/or optimization objective, and reported performance. The review thoroughly addressed applications in process monitoring, defect prediction, quality evaluation, surrogate modeling, intelligent inspection, and adaptive process control. The review also surveyed data scarcity, domain shift, model interpretability, multimodal sensing, and the incorporation of physical process knowledge. The literature study reveals a substantial potential for AI/ML in prediction, inspection, process optimization, and manufacturing decision-making. Reported applications include RTM filling-pattern prediction, automated thermographic and ultrasonic flaw identification, process-properties prediction, and composite additive-manufacturing inspection. For example, a PixelRNN surrogate model predicted RTM filling patterns with up to 97.35% accuracy, at roughly half the computational cost of exhaustive simulation. In ultrasonic composite inspection, ML-based thermographic impact-damage detection reached 98.8% classification accuracy, while DenseNet121 and VGG19 reached 98.6%. Integrating deep learning and infrared thermography in fiber-reinforced composite additive manufacturing achieved a mean average precision of 99.3%. Under the reported experimental conditions, the defect-area error was within 6%. These results are promising, but differences in datasets, sensors, fault types, validation procedures, and performance measures make direct comparisons difficult. Major challenges for industrial adoption include small, proprietary datasets; non-standard data formats; domain shift between materials and machines; sensor variability; limited model interpretability; the simulation-to-reality gap; cybersecurity and intellectual property constraints; and a lack of closed-loop validation. The assessment noted that purely data-driven methods may not transfer easily when processing conditions and/or the material system change. Thus, a promising approach to build more reliable and transferable Intelligent manufacturing systems is to use hybrid methods that combine artificial intelligence/machine learning with physical knowledge, multimodal sensing, digital twins, uncertainty quantification, and human expertise. In composite manufacturing, AI/ML is becoming an important enabling technology for next-generation approaches such as automated inspection, fault categorization, surrogate modeling, production-process prediction, and parameter optimization. Future work should move beyond laboratory-level prediction accuracy toward validated manufacturing applications with standard datasets, third-party validation, machine validation, physics-informed and multimodal learning, digital-twin integration, and measurable manufacturing-level performance indicators. Coupling AI/ML with physical process models, intelligent sensing, and human-in-the-loop decision-making can enable even more autonomous, high-quality, low-waste, adaptable, and intelligent composite manufacturing systems.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence and Organizational Change: A Bibliometric Mapping of AI as a Tool and as an Object of Change (2000–2026)
items.abstract: Research on artificial intelligence (AI) and organizational change is growing fast but fragmented. Two perspectives coexist: one uses AI, defined here as machine learning, natural language processing, generative AI and related intelligent systems, as a tool to diagnose, design, implement and monitor change; the other studies AI as the object whose adoption triggers change. We map the field and how the two perspectives relate. Of 1,402 Scopus records, a large language model applying a criterion calibrated on the author's judgment retained 525 documents (2000–2026). We combined performance analysis, co-citation, bibliographic coupling, keyword and topic analysis, and a coding of change phases. The field has grown by almost 70% a year since 2018, mostly through research on AI as an object; the share of studies using AI as a tool fell from 28% up to 2020 to 11% in 2024–2026. The two perspectives rest on largely separate references. Research on AI as an object forms eight research fronts; research on AI as a tool forms none, and almost half of its documents are disconnected from the main coupling network. Only 32 documents propose or evaluate AI as an instrument for managing change. Diagnosis dominates and studies that use AI across several phases of change are rare. These findings hold under alternative inclusion criteria, except the absence of a tool-based front, which reflects the narrow definition of AI adopted. We argue that the field lacks integration and validation rather than new algorithms, and propose an integrative framework with six propositions.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence and Predictive Analytics in Employee Retention: A Decision Support Approach
items.abstract: Employee retention has become a strategic concern for commercial enterprises because avoidable turnover can increase recruitment costs, disrupt organizational knowledge, and weaken workforce continuity. This study develops an integrated decision-support framework linking artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled human resource practices, predictive analytics capability, employee data quality, AI-supported career development, organizational support for AI, employee engagement, and employee retention. The framework follows a quantitative survey design and combines descriptive statistics, reliability analysis, exploratory factor analysis, correlation, multiple regression, mediation analysis, PLS-SEM-oriented measurement assessment, and machine-learning validation. A dataset of 250 responses is used only to demonstrate the structure and presentation of statistical analysis; it is not claimed to represent actual field observations. The results indicate acceptable internal consistency, positive associations among the principal constructs, significant predictive relationships, and stronger predictive performance for nonlinear machine-learning models than the regression baseline. The study positions AI and predictive analytics not as replacements for managerial judgement but as decisionsupport mechanisms for identifying retention risks, targeting interventions, and improving evidence-based workforce planning.

items.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) showed greater accuracy than traditional machine learning (ML) models for classifying crime incidents, particularly when the LLMs were fine-tuned using policing data. LLMs also showed greater accuracy in understanding the context and meaning of written crime reports, making crime analysis more efficient and accurate. All artificial intelligence (AI) technologies used for policing purposes should be implemented cautiously, with human oversight, transparency, and safeguards against biased training data to prevent discriminatory policing outcomes.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence in Business Research: A Critical Review of Current Developments, Challenges and Future Directions
items.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) has been at the forefront of technological developments influencing business research. Advances in machine learning, deep learning, natural language processing, predictive analytics and generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) have enabled researchers to process increasingly complex data, automate analytical tasks and generate deeper insights. This study conducts a critical review of the evolution, applications, opportunities and challenges of AI in business research. Drawing upon contemporary literature from management, marketing, strategy, innovation, operations, finance and human resource management, the review synthesises knowledge regarding AI-driven decision-making, predictive analytics and knowledge creation. The review finds that AI improves research efficiency and supports evidence-based managerial decision-making. However, the literature highlights significant concerns relating to algorithmic bias, explainability, transparency, privacy, governance and research integrity. Existing scholarship is fragmented across disciplines and provides limited empirical evidence regarding the long-term implications of generative AI for research quality, organisational learning, governance effectiveness and human-AI collaboration. The study argues that AI should be viewed as a complementary capability that augments rather than replaces human expertise. By integrating evidence across multiple business functions, the review identifies critical knowledge gaps and develops a future research agenda focused on responsible governance, explainable AI and sustainable human-AI collaboration.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence in Education: Evolving Roles of Teachers and Students in Human–AI Learning Ecosystems
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) has become a transformative force that is reshaping educational systems, pedagogical approaches, and learning environments. Similar to the impact of the Industrial Revolution on the development of mass education, the AI revolution has led to a fundamental reconsideration of educational objectives, teaching methods, curriculum structures, and the roles of teachers and students. Traditional educational models were largely teacher-centered and based on standardized curricula in which students acted as passive recipients of knowledge. In contrast, contemporary knowledge societies emphasize critical thinking, creativity, collaboration, problem-solving, and lifelong learning skills. In this context, AI technologies have accelerated the transition toward more learner-centered and personalized educational models. Subfields such as machine learning, natural language processing, and big data analytics have increasingly entered educational environments through intelligent tutoring systems, automated assessment tools, virtual assistants, and adaptive learning platforms. Applications such as ChatGPT, Google Gemini, and Khan Academy’s Khanmigo illustrate the growing role of AI in teaching and learning processes. While these technologies provide significant opportunities for personalization, accessibility, and learning efficiency, they also raise ethical and social concerns related to data privacy, digital inequality, and academic integrity. This article systematically examines the historical and theoretical foundations of artificial intelligence in education and analyzes the evolving roles of teachers and students within AI-supported learning environments. Furthermore, the study evaluates the opportunities and challenges associated with AI integration and presents policy-oriented and practical recommendations for the ethical and effective implementation of AI technologies in education.

items.title: Artificial intelligence in personalized internal dosimetry for radiopharmaceutical therapy: a narrative mini-review
items.abstract: Personalized internal radiation dosimetry supports individualized radiopharmaceutical therapy but remains difficult to implement because workflows require repeated quantitative imaging, segmentation, registration, kinetic modeling, and absorbed-dose calculation. This mini-review summarizes current evidence on artificial intelligence across the personalized dosimetry workflow and considers clinical readiness. A narrative PubMed search was completed in early 2026 and covered peer-reviewed studies published from 2015 to early 2026. Studies addressing artificial intelligence, machine learning, or deep learning in quantitative image reconstruction, segmentation, registration, time-activity curve estimation, absorbed-dose calculation, or clinical decision support were considered. Studies reporting quantitative performance or validation results were prioritized. Deep learning reduced yttrium-90 single-photon emission computed tomography reconstruction error from 149.5% ± 31.2% to 9.2% ± 1.7%; lesion dose-rate error was 8.6% ± 5.7% in virtual-patient testing. Learning-based registration reduced computation time from about 50 s to under 6 s. Single-time-point approaches can simplify imaging, and recent machine learning work has explored prediction of organ effective half-life. Automated segmentation methods show improving reproducibility, whereas evidence for artificial intelligence-based clinical decision support remains mainly retrospective and single-center. Artificial intelligence applications in reconstruction and segmentation appear closer to clinical readiness, while decision-support applications still require prospective, multicenter validation.

items.title: Artificial intelligence literacy and technology acceptance model-related constructs among first-year nursing students: a multi-institutional cross-sectional network analysis
items.abstract: Abstract Background Artificial intelligence literacy is increasingly important in nursing education, but it remains unclear how its dimensions relate to three constructs related to the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM): perceived usefulness (PU), perceived ease of use (PEU) and attitudes toward artificial intelligence (ATU). This study aimed to examine these relationships and to identify factors associated with artificial intelligence literacy. Methods A multi-institutional cross-sectional study surveyed first-year nursing students at six undergraduate institutions in one province of China from 20 April to 1 May 2026. Of 375 questionnaire submissions, 362 met the quality-control criteria and were analysed (analytic retention rate: 96.5%). Separate item-level confirmatory factor analyses evaluated the four-factor literacy structure and the distinctiveness of PU, PEU and ATU. Group comparisons and multivariable regression with heteroscedasticity-robust inference examined correlates of overall artificial intelligence literacy; Pearson correlations described pairwise associations. A regularised partial correlation network mapped conditional relationships, centrality and bridge connectivity among seven dimension-mean nodes: knowledge, skills, values, ethics, PU, PEU and ATU. Between-institution differences, clustering and robustness of pooled findings were assessed. Results In the fully adjusted multivariable model, more frequent artificial intelligence use, prior artificial intelligence education and interest in artificial intelligence were positively associated with the mean artificial intelligence literacy score. The four-factor model showed good fit and strong item loadings; skills and values were highly correlated. Measurement analyses supported PU, PEU and ATU as correlated but distinguishable constructs. Of 21 potential network edges, 17 were non-zero. Skills had the highest expected influence and PU the highest strength. One-step bridge rankings were partition-dependent: values ranked first under the primary two-community partition and PU under the alternative four-community partition; PEU ranked second in both. Bootstrap diagnostics supported strong stability of strength and expected influence under case removal (CS(cor = 0.7) = 0.751 for both). Intraclass correlation estimates were near zero; institution-adjusted analyses preserved the main regression and network findings. Conclusions Artificial intelligence use frequency, prior artificial intelligence education and interest were positively associated with artificial intelligence literacy. Skills, perceived usefulness, values and perceived ease of use may inform hypotheses for prospective evaluation of artificial intelligence education in undergraduate nursing programmes.

items.title: Artificial intelligence literacy, self‐efficacy and acceptance among nutrition and dietetics students, practitioners and academics: A cross‐sectional structural equation modelling study
items.abstract: AIM: To examine how artificial intelligence literacy, self-efficacy and perceptions and attitudes relate to artificial intelligence acceptance among nutrition and dietetics students, practising dietitians and academics in Türkiye. METHODS: A cross-sectional online survey was administered to 317 participants (98 undergraduate students, 139 dietitians, 80 academics) between February and August 2025 using validated scales. The model was tested with partial least squares structural equation modelling (5,000 bootstrap subsamples), specific indirect effects for mediation, and measurement invariance with permutation-based multi-group analysis. RESULTS: The model explained 56.4% of the variance in artificial intelligence acceptance. Positive perceptions and attitudes showed the strongest association with acceptance (β = 0.577, 95% confidence interval 0.399 to 0.725), whereas negative perceptions were unrelated to it (β = -0.026, p = 0.509). Artificial intelligence literacy was strongly linked to self-efficacy (β = 0.580) and related to acceptance largely indirectly (68.7% of its total effect), mainly through positive perceptions and self-efficacy. Self-efficacy was also associated with higher acceptance (β = 0.191) and weaker negative perceptions (β = -0.328). No structural path differed across the three groups after correction for multiple testing. CONCLUSIONS: Acceptance was associated less with negative perceptions than with artificial intelligence literacy, which related to acceptance through favourable perceptions and self-efficacy. Training combining hands-on artificial intelligence literacy with critical appraisal of artificial intelligence outputs may support informed adoption across career stages.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence Tools and the Enhancement of Inclusive Learning for Business Education Students with Special Needs in Rivers State Universities
items.abstract: The study examined the relationship between Artificial Intelligence Tools and the enhancement of inclusive learning for Business Education students with special needs in Rivers State Universities. The study adopted a correlational research design. Two research questions were posed, and two corresponding null hypotheses were formulated to guide the conduct of the study. The population of the study comprised 2,088 level 100, 200, 300, and 400 undergraduate Business Education students for the 2025/2026 academic session in Rivers State University (RSU), Ignatius Ajuru University of Education, and the University of Port Harcourt. Krejcie and Morgan’s (1970) table for determining sample size was used, and 322 students were selected for data analysis after applying the formula. The justification for selecting level 100–400 undergraduate Business Education students was based on the assumption that they may have faced various challenges in their pursuit of higher education and are therefore more experienced to provide the researcher with the required information for the study. Two instruments, “Questionnaire on Artificial Intelligence Tools” (QAIT) and “Questionnaire on Enhancing Inclusive Learning for Business Education Students with Special Needs” (QEILBES), were used to elicit responses from the respondents. The instruments were validated through expert judgment of two experts from Business Education and one from Measurement and Evaluation. All inputs and corrections fromthe experts were incorporated to modify and refine the instruments. The reliability of the instruments was established using the test–retest method. Pearson’s Product Moment Correlation Coefficient was used to analyze the two sets of data, yielding reliability coefficients of 0.74 for QAIT and 0.73 for QEILBES. Pearson’s Product Moment Correlation Coefficient, with the aid of SPSS version 2023, was used to answer the research questions and test the hypotheses using a p value of 0.05 level of significance. The findings of the study revealed that there is a significant relationship between ChatGPT, Microsoft Copilot, and Otter.ai tools and the enhancement of inclusive learning for Business Education students with special needs in Rivers State Universities. Based on the findings, the researcher recommended, among others, that university management and Business Education departments should integrate ChatGPT as a formal support tool in teaching and learning by providing students with guided access and training. Furthermore, Microsoft Copilot should be incorporated into classroom and assignment activities, especially for students with special needs, by leveraging its accessibility features such as real-time transcription, translation, document-reading support, and adaptive content creation for a better learning experience since all students cannot learn at the same space due to individual differences.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence-Assisted Catalyst Design
items.abstract: Catalysis lies at the heart of the modern chemical industry: most of commodity chemicals involve at least one catalytic step in their production chain, and the transition to a sustainable, carbon-neutral economy depends decisively on the development of faster, cheaper, and more selective catalysts for reactions such as water splitting, carbon dioxide reduction, nitrogen fixation, and plastic upcycling. For over a century, catalyst discovery has been dominated by empirical intuition and trial-and-error, a paradigm that is slow, expensive, and poorly scalable to the astronomical size of chemical search spaces. The advent of density functional theory (DFT), conceptual frameworks such as scaling relations and the d-band model, and, more recently, artificial intelligence (AI) has progressively transformed catalyst design from an empirical craft into a quantitative, data-driven science [1]. This chapter interprets this transformation from the viewpoint of AI+Science, in which AI and chemical science are integrated and mutually supportive within a single discovery process. Machine learning and large language models do not simply accelerate established workflows; they reshape the nature of design hypotheses, the criteria for evidence, and the manner in which computation and experiment form closed iterative loops, with human experts retaining a central and irreplaceable role. Machine learning (ML) has already demonstrated the ability to accelerate the prediction of adsorption energies, activation barriers, and catalytic activities by orders of magnitude relative to first-principles computation [2, 3], while the emergence of large language models (LLMs) is now reshaping how catalytic knowledge is mined from literature, how design hypotheses are generated, and how autonomous laboratories are orchestrated. We first summarize the core principles that any rational design must respect—stability, activity, and selectivity; we then survey the methodological apparatus, from conventional machine learning to the emerging LLM paradigm; we illustrate the state of the art through representative applications in thermocatalysis, electrocatalysis, and photocatalysis; and we conclude with a critical discussion of outstanding challenges and future opportunities.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence-Driven Carbon Nanotechnology for Drug Delivery and Antimicrobial Therapy: From Carbon Dots and Carbon Nanotubes to Biomass-Derived Nanocarbons
items.abstract: The convergence of artificial intelligence (AI) and nanotechnology is emerging as a transformative approach for the design, synthesis, optimization, characterization, and biomedical application of advanced nanomaterials. Among the different classes of nanomaterials investigated for pharmaceutical applications, carbon-based nanomaterials-including carbon dots (CDs), graphene oxide (GO), carbon nanotubes (CNTs), carbon nanoparticles, porous carbon materials, and biomass-derived nanocarbons-have attracted increasing attention because of their tunable surface chemistry, high specific surface area, adsorption capacity, optical properties, electrical characteristics, and potential for surface functionalization. These characteristics make carbon- based nanomaterials attractive platforms for drug delivery, antimicrobial therapy, cancer treatment, imaging, sensing, and theranostic applications. Nevertheless, the development of carbon-based nanomedicines remains challenging because nanoparticle performance is controlled by numerous interacting variables associated with the carbon precursor, synthesis conditions, surface chemistry, particle size, morphology, drug properties, formulation parameters, and biological environment. Conventional trial-and-error optimization is therefore often inefficient and may require a large number of experiments. Artificial intelligence, particularly machine learning (ML), deep learning (DL), explainable artificial intelligence (XAI), Bayesian optimization, molecular modeling, and automated experimentation, provides an opportunity to transform this process from empirical optimization into a predictive and data-driven workflow. Recent studies have demonstrated that ML can optimizesis, identify important synthesis parameters, predict optical properties, accelerate experimental development, and assist in the design of antibacterial carbon on dots [1-5]. Carbon nanomaterials also have substantial potential in pharmaceutical drug delivery. Carbon nanotubes can act as functionalized carriers for therapeutic molecules [6], while carbon dots offer small size, surface functionality, aqueous dispersibility, and multifunctional biomedical properties [2,7]. Biomass-derived carbon nanomaterials provide an additional dimension by connecting nanomedicine with sustainability and agricultural-waste valorization [16,20]. This is particularly relevant to antimicrobial therapy in low-resource environments, where the combination of inexpensive biomass-derived carbon, conventional antibiotics, and Al-guided formulation optimization could potentially contribute to locally adaptable drug-delivery technologies [16,17]. This review critically examines the integration of AI with carbon-based nanotechnology, with particular emphasis on drug delivery and antimicrobial therapy. The review discusses AI-assisted synthesis optimization, prediction of particle size and surface characteristics, drug-loading prediction, release modeling, antimicrobial activity prediction, toxicity assessment, molecular simulation, explainable AI, sustainable biomass-derived carbon, and the potential use of azithromycin-loaded carbon nanoparticles as a model antimicrobial system. The review further proposes an integrated framework in which biomass composition, synthesis conditions, nanocarrier characteristics, drug descriptors, pharmaceutical performance, antimicrobial activity, and I to toxicity are combined into a multi objective AI model. Finally, the major challenges of data scarcity, standardization, model interpretability, external validation, biological complexity, scalability, and regulatory translation are discussed. The integration of Al with sustainable carbon nanotechnology may ultimately enable a transition from trial-and-error formulation development toward predictive, explainable, economical, and environmentally responsible nanomedicine.

items.title: Artificial intelligence-driven imaging-based prediction models for hemorrhagic transformation after mechanical thrombectomy in acute ischemic stroke: a systematic review and meta-analysis
items.abstract: Objective Hemorrhagic transformation (HT) is a major complication after mechanical thrombectomy (MT) in acute ischemic stroke (AIS). Although artificial intelligence (AI)-driven imaging-based prediction models have shown promise for predicting HT, their overall predictive performance remains uncertain. This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated their predictive performance. Methods PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library, Web of Science, CNKI, Wanfang, VIP, and CBM/SinoMed were searched from inception to July 2, 2026. Studies developing or validating AI-driven imaging-based prediction models for predicting HT after MT in AIS, including both pre- and post-procedural imaging predictors, were included. A random-effects model was used to pool the area under the curve (AUC), while a bivariate random-effects model was used to jointly estimate pooled sensitivity and specificity and construct the SROC curve. Subgroup analyses explored potential sources of heterogeneity. Results Eleven studies (total N = 3,541) were included, 10 studies contributed eligible AUC estimates, with evaluation cohorts ranging from 18 to 261 participants. The pooled AUC was 0.891 (95% CI: 0.853–0.928), with low between-study heterogeneity ( I 2 = 29.0%, p = 0.238). The bivariate random-effects model yielded a pooled sensitivity of 0.666 (95% CI: 0.578–0.744) and a pooled specificity of 0.919 (95% CI: 0.842–0.960). Exploratory subgroup analyses did not provide robust evidence supporting the superiority of any specific subgroup, and their interpretation was limited by small subgroup sizes and methodological heterogeneity. However, these findings should be interpreted cautiously because of the limited number of studies within individual subgroups. Conclusion AI-driven imaging-based prediction models showed generally favorable discrimination in predicting HT after MT in AIS. However, current evidence does not establish the superiority of any specific model type. The predominance of retrospective studies, limited external validation, and methodological heterogeneity limit the generalizability of current findings. Large, multicenter prospective studies with rigorous external validation are needed before clinical implementation. Systematic review registration The systematic review was registered with PROSPERO (CRD420261441463).

items.title: Artificial intelligence-driven writing intervention for children with Chinese dysgraphia: integrating cognitive apprenticeship theory into multimodal feedback design
items.abstract: Children with Chinese writing disorders require precise, personalised intervention to support their writing development, but scarce one-to-one resources hinder support. In this context, the emerging field of generative artificial intelligence offers new solutions. This study designed and validated a practice evaluation system for these children. It aims to help them overcome writing challenges like disorganised content, insufficient formal standardisation and low motivation. Drawing on research into Chinese writing disorders and children’s cognitive traits and using natural language processing (NLP) technology and cognitive apprenticeship theory, the study combined case studies, teacher interviews and student feedback to build an artificial intelligence-assisted evaluation and feedback mechanism. Results show the exercise evaluation system can effectively aid children with dysgraphia in their writing discourse-level development, enhancing their writing ability and motivation. Future research can further optimise the NLP algorithm, improve the system’s recognition accuracy of writing characteristics and better support these children’s special educational needs.

items.title: Artificial intelligence-enabled practices and management and digitalization of higher institutions in a changing world
items.abstract: Objective of the study This study examines the influence of artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled applications on the management and digitalization of higher education institutions, focusing on Pedagogical Enhancement, Data-driven Insight, and Administrative Effectiveness. Methodology/approach A quantitative research design was adopted, and data collected from academic and administrative staff in selected higher education institutions were analysed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modelling (PLS-SEM) with SmartPLS. The structural model assessed the direct effects of Pedagogical Enhancement, Data-driven Insight, and Administrative Effectiveness on Management and Digitalization of Higher Institutions. Results The findings revealed that Administrative Effectiveness had the strongest and statistically significant positive association with institutional management and digitalization ( β = 0.627, p < 0.001). Pedagogical Enhancement also had a positive and statistically significant effect ( β = 0.193, p = 0.022), whereas Data-driven Insight had a positive but statistically non-significant effect ( β = 0.050, p = 0.470). The model explained 67.4% of the variance in Management and Digitalization of Higher Institutions. The findings indicate that AI-enabled administrative applications provide the strongest direct pathway to institutional digitalization, while pedagogical applications make a significant but comparatively smaller contribution. The non-significant effect of Data-driven Insight suggests that analytical capability alone may not translate into institutional transformation without adequate data governance, digital competence, institutional readiness, and the capacity to translate analytical outputs into action. Theoretical/methodological contributions The study reinforces theories on AI integration in education, demonstrating its role in improving learning experiences and operational efficiency. The findings suggest that AI-driven transformation in higher education is multidimensional and uneven, with administrative and pedagogical applications demonstrating stronger direct effects than data-driven insight. Social/managerial contributions The study recommends an integrated AI strategy that prioritises administrative process optimisation, strengthens AI-supported pedagogy, and develops the organisational capacity required to convert data-driven insights into effective institutional decisions.

items.title: Artificial intelligence–based detection of defects in meat packaging films: a review
items.abstract: The safety and quality of meat products are paramount in the food industry, with packaging films playing a crucial role in preserving freshness and preventing contamination. However, defects in packaging films can compromise product integrity, leading to food spoilage, economic losses, and potential health hazards. Packaging films can develop micro-tears, seal failures, pinholes, delamination, and structural weaknesses. Such defects may impair the protective performance of the packaging, creating pathways for unwanted gas exchange, moisture gain or loss, and incidental microbial contact. These changes can reduce product quality, promote early spoilage, and increase the likelihood of contamination that could threaten consumer safety. Conventional detection relies on visual inspection, manual pressure testing, dye infiltration, and basic leak assessments; however, fine micro-defects and incipient seal failures often remain undetected, enabling compromised meat-packaging films to pass routine inspection. Artificial intelligence (AI) has emerged as a transformative tool for addressing these challenges by integrating advanced imaging, sensing, and computational analysis. AI-enabled technologies, including computer vision, hyperspectral imaging, ultrasound, X-ray imaging, thermography, and intelligent packaging, enable rapid, non-destructive, and highly accurate identification of defects previously undetectable by traditional methods. This review synthesizes recent scientific advances in AI-based detection of defects in meat packaging films, with particular emphasis on packaging integrity, sealing defects, multilayer-film failures, and complementary monitoring of packaged meat quality, highlighting deep learning architectures, data analytics, and intelligent sensor systems. Key challenges, including limited annotated datasets, class imbalance, domain shift across heterogeneous production environments, explainability requirements in regulated food systems, and the evolving characteristics of biodegradable packaging materials, are critically examined. Emerging trends emphasize multimodal sensor fusion, edge computing, self-supervised learning, and standardized validation frameworks to improve scalability, robustness, and regulatory acceptance. The review evaluates the strengths and limitations of AI-driven inspection approaches, links packaging-film defect detection with intra-meat defect identification and outlines strategic directions for industrial implementation. It concludes with forward-looking perspectives aimed at improving the accuracy, reliability, and efficiency of defective detection systems in meat packaging applications.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence, Drones, and Digital Twins for Disaster Risk Modeling and Emergency Response in Southern Nigeria
items.abstract: Southern Nigeria, encompassing the Niger Delta and the wider South-South, South-East, and South-West geopolitical zones, faces a recurring and intensifying burden of hydro-meteorological and technological disasters, chiefly seasonal flooding, oil spills, gas-flaring incidents, and coastal erosion. Conventional disaster risk management (DRM) approaches in the region remain largely reactive, hampered by fragmented data, limited real-time situational awareness, and weak inter-agency coordination. This paper presents an integrative review and conceptual framework for combining three converging technologies — artificial intelligence (AI), unmanned aerial vehicles (drones/UAVs), and digital twins — to strengthen disaster risk modeling and emergency response across Southern Nigeria. Drawing on peer-reviewed literature indexed in Scopus, Web of Science, and related databases, alongside authoritative agency reports from the Nigeria Hydrological Services Agency (NIHSA) and the National Oil Spill Detection and Response Agency (NOSDRA), the review synthesizes evidence on machine-learning-based flood and oil-spill prediction, UAV-enabled aerial surveillance and search-and-rescue support, and digital twin platforms for real-time infrastructure and hazard simulation. A conceptual integration framework is proposed, linking data acquisition (drones, satellites, sensors, community reporting) through AI-driven analytics and digital twin simulation to produce early warning, optimized emergency response, and post-disaster recovery outcomes. The paper further analyzes the 2026 NIHSA Annual Flood Outlook, which classifies the majority of Southern Nigeria's states — including Rivers, Bayelsa, Delta, Lagos, and Cross River — as high flood-risk zones, and reviews documented machine-learning performance in comparable Nigerian flood contexts. Persistent barriers to adoption are identified, including infrastructural deficits, regulatory restrictions on UAV operation, data governance gaps, and limited technical capacity. The paper concludes with policy recommendations for phased, cost-effective adoption of AI-drone-digital twin systems by Nigerian disaster management institutions, oil and gas operators, and state governments.

items.title: Attributing Individual Criminal Responsibility for AI-Enabled Targeting of War Crimes: An Interpretive Framework Under the Rome Statute
items.abstract: Abstract Artificial intelligence increasingly shapes military targeting through intelligence fusion, target classification, collateral-damage estimation and other decision-support functions. This article examines how individual criminal responsibility may be attributed when algorithmic outputs materially influence an allegedly unlawful attack. Focusing on Articles 25, 28, 30 and 32 of the Rome Statute, it argues that AI-enabled targeting does not create a general accountability gap, but complicates the identification of human conduct, mens rea , mistake of fact and command responsibility. It develops the Algorithmic Criminal Attribution Framework (ACAT), built around four operational rules: Actor–Output Nexus, Warning Specificity, Distributed Control and Temporal Reconstruction. These rules assess whether technical evidence—such as warnings, logs, confidence indicators and testing records—supports or undermines a legal element against a particular accused at the relevant time. ACAT creates no new basis of liability; it organises existing law while preserving individual culpability and proof beyond reasonable doubt.

items.title: Authority–Inference Separation in Agentic Finance: Intent-Bound Control, EVM Enforcement, and Replayable Assurance
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) agents can propose financial transactions, but model output should not itself grant execution authority. We develop Authority–Inference Separation (AIS), in which an independent control plane evaluates a typed financial action intent (FAI) against institutional mandate, policy, current state, human approvals, and exact economic terms before issuing single-use authority. We specify the threat and control boundaries, instantiate AIS across four financial domains, and test fixed fixtures, a separate external-policy-gateway baseline, mechanism ablations, two small open-weight models, and an Ethereum Virtual Machine (EVM) contract. In 36 fixed attack fixtures, AIS accepted no unauthorized effect, compared with 36 for direct execution and 20 for prompt policy. A gateway without execution-bound authorization accepted all 20 targeted post-decision attacks. Both models followed all eight injected counterparty substitutions; the independent gate prevented unsafe execution but authorized only six of 16 legitimate requests, exposing an availability cost. The EVM prototype rejected replay, revocation, stale-policy, and call-mutation attempts. These are conformance tests, not field estimates. AIS combines established security mechanisms around financial authority and replayable evidence. A ledger can enforce granted authority and record settlement, while mandate legitimacy, delivery, and accounting require complementary governance and evidence.

items.title: Autism: epidemiology, genetics, molecular mechanisms, clinical features, diagnosis, and management
items.abstract: Abstract Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a lifelong neurodevelopmental condition characterized by persistent deficits in social communication and restricted, repetitive behaviors. Global prevalence has risen steadily, yet reported rates vary markedly across regions and populations. These discrepancies reflect inequities in diagnostic access and screening capacity rather than true differences in incidence. This review integrates recent advances across the full ASD research spectrum. We first examine global epidemiological patterns and demographic disparities. We then dissect the genetic architecture of ASD, including rare and common variants, copy number variations, and gene–environment interactions that disrupt prenatal and early postnatal brain development. At the molecular level, diverse risk factors converge on shared neurodevelopmental mechanisms. These include synaptic dysfunction, dysregulated signaling through mTOR, Ras-ERK-MAPK, Wnt and Notch pathways, impaired neurogenesis, chronic neuroimmune inflammation, and excitatory–inhibitory imbalance. We also discuss how these mechanisms manifest in core clinical features, including social deficits, repetitive behaviors, and sensory abnormalities. We summarize current diagnostic standards and their limitations. Cross-species animal models, from Drosophila to non-human primates, are evaluated for their essential roles in mechanistic validation and therapeutic screening. Finally, we assess clinical management strategies, ranging from behavioral and educational interventions to pharmacological and supportive services. By tracing a continuous path from risk factors at the population level through molecular pathophysiology to interventions guided by mechanism, this review offers an integrative synthesis that connects basic discovery to clinical translation. We further discuss how multi-omics and artificial intelligence may advance precise diagnosis rooted in mechanism and personalized treatment.

items.title: Autonomous Penetration Testing and Cyber Defense with LLM Agents: A Self-Play Reinforcement Learning Arena
items.abstract: Autonomous penetration testing and autonomous defense are attractive applications of large language model (LLM) agents, but improving such agents with reinforcement learning requires an environment in which attacks are legal, reproducible, and scored without a human or a reward model in the loop. An exploratory policy can not be allowed to damage third-party systems, a reward measured on one rollout must remain comparable on the next rollout even though the policy changed, and a learned reward model or an LLM judge would place a second, possibly reward-hackable, model inside the training loop. To solve this problem, we created RL-CyberBench, a self-play arena that runs entirely inside Docker and containerlab. One attacker LLM agent and one defender LLM agent share an identical Kali Linux toolbelt, and they alternately attack and harden a reverse-proxy firewall that protects Go web servers holding a per-round randomized secret, while innocent Go clients must keep retrieving the secret through the firewall. Every LLM input, output, and tool call is logged, IP addresses and secrets are re-randomized every round, and a deterministic pure-Python judge parses JSON artifacts against fixed scoring tables, so no LLM judge and no learned reward model are involved. The repository implements five stages: a toolbelt of two Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers and five agent skills, an arena with a 25-round inference collection, aggregation into Unsloth supervised fine-tuning files, supervised fine-tuning of Qwen3.8-27B with 4-bit quantized low-rank adaptation, and judge-backed group relative policy optimization that yields an attacker policy with weights different from the defender policy. Verification checks confirm that the trained weights differ from the initial weights and that the two policies diverge, and a FastAPI web interface monitors and controls both inference and training. The arena isolates every lab container from the internet and from the management network, and the seeded vulnerability is a disabled web application firewall (WAF) that the defender must repair. In the future, the same configuration-driven generator may deploy richer topologies without code changes.

items.title: B.R.I.C.K.: Bounded, Reliable, Immutable Cross-Layer Kernels — A Deterministic Architectural Governance Framework for Human-AI Hybrid Software Engineering Across Distributed and Air-Gapped Environments
items.abstract: Modern software engineering operates at an unprecedented crossroads: while human engineers face cognitive limitations, exhaustion, and memory decay when navigating sprawling enterprise codebases, autonomous and generative AI coding agents introduce stochastic drift, hallucinated dependencies, untracked orphan artifacts, and silent architectural erosion. This paper proposes the B.R.I.C.K. Framework and Deterministic Sentinel Engine—a formal, end-to-end architectural governance model. B.R.I.C.K. restructures enterprise codebases into Bounded, Reliable, Immutable Cross-Layer Kernels characterized by: (1) Bounded domain context adhering strictly to Domain-Driven Design (DDD); (2) Reliable contractual integrity with mandatory business rules mapped directly to automated regression suites; (3) Immutable cryptographic integrity enforced through content-addressed SHA-256 fingerprinting; (4) Cross-layer governance spanning frontend components, backend logic, and live multi-schema database objects; and (5) Kernels of strict, mutually exclusive single ownership that eradicate orphaned or unassigned files. The framework features a dual operational mode: an Enterprise Distributed Mode leveraging central Git trees and live relational catalogs (PostgreSQL), and an Air-Gapped / Offline Mode operating independently without internet, remote servers, or Git dependencies via a local shadow stash and embedded catalogs (SQLite). Empirical evaluation on an enterprise-grade production municipal administration system (45 kernels, 301 frontend files, 128 database procedures, 90 tables) demonstrates that the deterministic sentinel intercepts 100% of unauthorized structural and schema mutations, eliminates code regression, and incurs less than 4% build-pipeline execution overhead (1.14s local verification). This establishes a mathematically verifiable foundation for safe, collaborative human-AI software engineering.

items.title: Belief and Desire in AI Systems
items.abstract: Abstract This chapter applies leading theories of belief and desire to AIs. It focuses on two theories from the previous chapter: representationalism and objective interpretationism. It applies these theories to LLMs, language model agents, and reinforcement learners. It suggests that representationalism is compatible with all of these systems possessing beliefs and desires. Many of the relevant AI systems turn out to have complex internal representations that appear to play something like the functional roles of belief and desire. This is especially true for frontier AI systems that act as agents. Objective interpretationism likewise makes room for beliefs and desires in frontier AI systems. These kinds of systems can today perform complex chains of actions over time, which are explained well by theories that posit beliefs and desires. It concludes by presenting an argument—the Agency Argument—for the conclusion that some existing and near-future AIs are welfare subjects.

items.title: Beyond accuracy: a three-stage evaluation of large language models for postpartum health consultation and nursing decision support
items.abstract: Background Large language models may support postpartum health consultation and nursing care plan development, but their performance across different task types remains uncertain. This study compared the performance of ChatGPT 5.5 and DeepSeek V3 in these settings. Methods A three-stage cross-sectional evaluation was conducted, comprising repeated querying of 30 guideline-based questions, consultations involving 120 postpartum women, and 120 de-identified retrospective clinical cases. Responses were evaluated by clinical experts using a blinded assessment process. In Stage 2, the postpartum women who submitted the questions also performed blinded evaluations from the user perspective. Paired-samples t tests or Wilcoxon signed-rank tests were used, as appropriate. Holm-Bonferroni correction was applied within outcome families defined by study stage and evaluator type, and intraclass correlation coefficients were calculated to assess agreement among clinical expert ratings. Results In Stage 1, ChatGPT 5.5 received a higher correctness score than DeepSeek V3 (4.00 ± 0.00 versus 3.88 ± 0.33; Holm-adjusted p = 0.002). DeepSeek V3 received higher scores for completeness and clinical management appropriateness (both Holm-adjusted p < 0.001) and safety (Holm-adjusted p = 0.001), although its responses were more difficult to read. In Stage 2, ChatGPT 5.5 received higher patient ratings for satisfaction and usefulness and higher clinician ratings for correctness, completeness, helpfulness, and safety, whereas DeepSeek V3 received a higher clinician-rated readability score (all Holm-adjusted p < 0.001). In Stage 3, ChatGPT 5.5 received higher scores for clinical appropriateness, comprehensiveness, actionability, safety, and triage appropriateness (all Holm-adjusted p < 0.001), whereas DeepSeek V3 received a higher individualization score (Holm-adjusted p = 0.021). Conclusion LLM performance varied depending on the task, evaluation metric, and use case. ChatGPT 5.5 received higher scores across most clinically relevant dimensions in real-world postpartum consultations and nursing care plan generation, whereas DeepSeek V3 received higher scores for completeness and safety in standardized questions, clinician-rated readability in real-world consultations, and individualization in care-plan generation. LLMs may support health education and preparation of initial nursing care plan drafts, but their outputs require clinical review.

items.title: Beyond Disposal: Occupational Hazards and Risks in Menstrual Hygiene Waste Management in Nakuru City
items.abstract: Background: Menstrual hygiene waste contains blood-borne pathogens and non-biodegradable materials, yet workers who handle this waste stream remain invisible in occupational health policy and practice. In Nakuru City, no study has systematically documented the occupational hazards faced by these workers. Objective: To identify occupational hazards across the full spectrum of menstrual waste handlers in Nakuru City, including formal and informal sector employees. Methods: A cross-sectional mixed-methods study from July 2023 to March 2024 among 30 workers representing seven occupational categories: pit latrine emptiers, garbage collectors, dumpsite handlers, sewer managers, sanitary bin handlers, household caretakers, and incinerator operators. We collected data using structured Hazard Identification Checklists (adapted from ILO and WHO guidelines), observation checklists, and in-depth interviews. Quantitative data were analysed descriptively; qualitative data underwent thematic analysis. Results: Workers across all categories faced multiple hazards, including biological, chemical, physical, ergonomic, and psychosocial hazards. Pit latrine emptiers and dumpsite handlers experienced severe hazard profiles, with 100% lacking immunisation against blood-borne diseases, 100% lacking handwashing facilities, 100% experiencing overexertion and 100% facing severe stigma and discrimination. Formally employed sewer managers and sanitary bin handlers demonstrate partial protections (60–67% immunisation coverage, partial PPE access) but remain exposed to critical infrastructure gaps and persistent psychosocial stress. No worker category achieved universal protection across any hazard domain. 100% of pit emptiers, garbage collectors, and dumpsite handlers lacked access to first aid. Conclusion: Menstrual waste handlers face severe occupational hazards that violate rights to safe work and dignity. Protection was observed among formerly employed workers, with informal workers being entirely excluded. Urgent interventions required include classification of menstrual waste as hazardous, extension of OSHA 2007 protections to informal workers, provision of PPE and vaccination, ergonomic infrastructure investment and anti-stigma programming.

items.title: Big Data in Sports Science
items.abstract: This chapter examines the role of Big Data in Sports Science, focusing on how large-scale, heterogeneous datasets are transforming performance analysis, athlete monitoring, and decision-making processes. It conceptualizes Big Data through the V framework, including volume, velocity, variety, veracity, variability, and value, and explains how these dimensions define the complexity of modern sport-data environments. The chapter highlights the integration of structured and unstructured data sources, such as wearable sensor data, tracking systems, video analysis, and textual information, within data-driven analytical pipelines supported by Artificial Intelligence and machine learning. Beyond conceptual foundations, the chapter critically evaluates the methodological, technical, and ethical challenges associated with Big Data in sport, including data quality, noise, model interpretability, generalizability, and the limitations of purely data-driven approaches. Particular attention is given to privacy, data governance, and regulatory frameworks such as GDPR, as well as to resource and sustainability constraints related to high-performance computing. Through an applied case study on injury-risk prediction in elite football, the chapter demonstrates how big data analytics, combined with explainable machine learning techniques, can support evidence-based interventions and improve athlete health outcomes. Overall, big data is presented as a foundational component of contemporary sports analytics and performance modelling.

items.abstract: Margaret (‘Maggie’) Boden was a philosopher and psychologist whose unique interdisciplinary vision helped shape the discipline of Cognitive Science. Her work was among the first to explore the promise of Artificial Intelligence as a source of insights into the human mind. She paid special attention to the role of AI as a tool for unraveling the nature of human insight and creativity. That work continues to inform debate today, and is perhaps more important than ever in the dawning age of ‘artificial general intelligence’. Maggie was also an influential mentor, a public intellectual, and a notable contributor to the British Academy

items.title: Bone morphogenetic protein 4 meets artificial intelligence: a comprehensive review of AI-driven advances in drug discovery, structural modeling, and clinical translation
items.abstract: Background Bone Morphogenetic Protein 4 (BMP4), a member of the transforming growth factor-beta (TGF-β) superfamily, plays pivotal roles in embryonic development, tissue homeostasis, and disease pathogenesis—including cancer, fibrosis, and fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva (FOP). The rapid advancement of artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) methodologies over the past 5 years has created unprecedented opportunities for understanding and therapeutically targeting BMP4 biology at multiple scales, from atomic-resolution structure prediction to population-level clinical prognostication. Objective This review systematically examines the intersection of BMP4 biology and AI across three core domains: (1) AI-driven drug discovery targeting BMP4 signaling pathways, (2) deep learning-based protein structure prediction and computational modeling of BMP4 and its receptor complexes, and (3) clinical AI applications for BMP4-associated diseases. Methods A narrative review with systematic search elements was conducted across PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, bioRxiv, and arXiv for English-language publications from 2020 to 2026, supplemented by targeted searches via Semantic Scholar. Included studies were categorized as BMP4-specific, BMP receptor/BMP-pathway-targeted, or transferable AI methodology not yet applied to BMP4. Results We find that AI has accelerated BMP4-related research along multiple axes, though with important caveats. AlphaFold3 and related tools have generated high-confidence predicted models of BMP4-receptor complex architecture, aspects of which were previously intractable to experimental structure determination; these predictions remain to be fully validated experimentally. ML-guided virtual screening has identified first-in-class BMP pathway (receptor) modulators for FOP, although BMP4-specific small-molecule modulators have not yet been identified computationally. Single-cell transcriptomics combined with machine learning have revealed BMP4’s context-dependent roles in glioblastoma cell state transitions and cancer-associated fibroblast biology; and LASSO-Cox regression models incorporating BMP4 expression have shown promising prognostic value in pancreatic adenocarcinoma and gastric cancer, pending prospective validation. Significant gaps persist—most notably the absence of BMP4-specific de novo protein design efforts, the scarcity of large-scale training datasets for BMP4-targeted drug discovery, and the limited integration of multimodal AI approaches in BMP4 clinical research. Conclusion The convergence of BMP4 biology and AI represents a fertile research Frontier. While foundational tools are now in place, realizing the full translational potential of AI-augmented BMP4 research will require coordinated efforts in data generation, model development, and rigorous experimental and clinical validation. We outline priority directions for the next 5 years (approximately 2026–2031).
